# Job Chapter 39 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 431r–431v

---

**39:1** "Do-you-know [hayada'ta] the-time [et] the-mountain-goats [ya'alei-sela] give-birth [leled]? Do-you-watch [tishmor] the-calving of-the-deer [ayalot]? **39:2** Do-you-count [tispor] the-months [yerachim] they-fulfill [temallena]? And-do-you-know [veyada'at] the-time [et] of-their-giving-birth [lidtanah]? **39:3** They-crouch [tikhrana], they-bring-forth [tefallatnah] their-young [yaldeihen], their-labor-pains [chevleihem] they-send-away [teshallechna]. **39:4** Their-young [beneihem] grow-strong [yachlimu], they-grow-up [yirbu] in-the-open-field [ba-bar]; they-go-out [yatse'u] and-do-not return [ve-lo-shavu] to-them [lamo].

**39:5** Who sent-out [shillach] the-wild-donkey [pere] free [chofshi]? And-the-bonds of-the-wild-donkey [arod], who loosed [pittea'ch]? **39:6** Whose home [beito] I-made [samti] the-steppe [aravah], and-its-dwelling [u-mishkenotav] the-salt-land [melechah]. **39:7** It-laughs [yis'chaq] at-the-tumult of-the-city [hamon qiryah]; the-shouts of-the-driver [teshu'ot noges] it-does-not hear [lo yishma]. **39:8** The-range of-the-mountains [yetur harim] [is] its-pasture [mir'ehu], and-after every green-thing [yaraq] it-searches [yidhrosh].

**39:9** Will-the-wild-ox [re'em] be-willing [yoveh] to-serve-you [avedekha]? Or-will-it-spend-the-night [yalin] at your-manger [al-avusekha]? **39:10** Can-you-bind [ha-tiqshor] the-wild-ox [re'em] in-the-furrow [ba-telem] with-its-rope [avoto]? Or-will-it-harrow [yesadded] the-valleys [amaqim] after-you [acharekha]? **39:11** Will-you-trust [ha-tivtach] in-it because its-strength [kocho] [is] great [rav]? And-will-you-leave [ve-ta'azov] to-it your-labor [yegi'akha]? **39:12** Will-you-rely [ha-ta'amin] on-it to-return [yashiv] your-seed [zar'ekha] and-to-gather [ve-gornekha] to-your-threshing-floor [ya'esof]?

**39:13** The-wing of-the-ostriches [kanaf-renanim] beats-joyously [ne'elasah]; is-it the-pinion [evrah] of-the-stork [chasidah] and-feathers [ve-notsah]? **39:14** For she-abandons [ta'azov] her-eggs [beitseha] to-the-ground [la-arets], and-on-the-dust [ve-al-afar] she-warms-them [techammen]. **39:15** And-she-forgets [va-tishkach] that a-foot [regel] may-crush-them [tezureha], and-a-beast of-the-field [chayyat ha-sadeh] may-trample-them [tedusheha]. **39:16** She-treats-harshly [hiqshi'ach] her-young [baneha] as-not hers [le-lo-lah]; in-vain [la-riq] [is] her-labor [yegia'ah], without fear [beli-fachad].

**39:17** For God [Eloah] made-her-forget [hishshahh] wisdom [chokhmah], and-did-not give-her-a-share [lo chalaq] in-understanding [ba-binah]. **39:18** At-the-time she-flaps-aloft [tamri], she-laughs [tis'chaq] at-the-horse [la-sus] and-its-rider [ve-le-rokhevo].

**39:19** Do-you-give [ha-titten] to-the-horse [la-sus] strength [gevurah]? Do-you-clothe [talbish] its-neck [tsavvaro] with-a-mane [ra'amah]? **39:20** Do-you-make-it-leap [tar'ishennu] like-a-locust [ka-arbeh]? The-splendor [hod] of-its-snorting [nachroh] [is] terror [eimah]. **39:21** It-paws [yachperu] in-the-valley [ba-emeq] and-rejoices [yasis] in-strength [be-choach]; it-goes-out [yetse] to-meet [liqrat] the-weapons [nasheq].

**39:22** It-laughs [yis'chaq] at-fear [le-fachad] and-is-not dismayed [ve-lo yechat]; and-does-not turn-back [ve-lo yashuv] from-the-face of-the-sword [mi-penei-charev]. **39:23** Upon-it rattles [tir'aneh] the-quiver [ashpah], the-blade [lahav] of-the-spear [chanit] and-the-javelin [ve-khidon]. **39:24** With-shaking [be-ra'ash] and-rage [ve-rogez] it-swallows [yegamme] the-ground [erets]; and-does-not stand-still [ve-lo ya'amin] at-the-sound of-the-horn [qol shofar]. **39:25** At-the-blast of-the-horn [bedei shofar] it-says [yomar], "Aha [he'ach]!" And-from-afar [me-rachoq] it-smells [yariach] the-battle [milchamah], the-thunder [ra'am] of-the-commanders [sarim] and-the-war-cry [u-teru'ah].

**39:26** Is-it by-your-understanding [mi-binatekha] the-hawk [nets] soars [ya'aver], spreading [yifros] its-wings [kenafav] to-the-south [le-teiman]? **39:27** Or-at your-command [al-pikha] the-eagle [nesher] mounts-up [yagbi'ah] and-makes [yasim] its-nest [qinno] on-high [yarum]? **39:28** On-the-cliff [sela] it-dwells [yishkon] and-lodges [vayitlonnan], upon the-tooth of-the-cliff [al-shen-sela] and-the-stronghold [u-metsudah]. **39:29** From-there it-searches-for [chaphar] food [okhel]; its-eyes [einav] gaze [yabbitu] from-afar [le-merachoq]. **39:30** And-its-young [ve-efrochhav] drink-up [yela'a'u] blood [dam]; and-where the-slain [chalalim] [are], there it [is] [sham hu]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.9 — "wild ox":** Hebrew *re'em* — not a domesticated ox but the now-extinct aurochs (*Bos primigenius*), a massive wild bovine. The KJV "unicorn" derives from the Septuagint *monokeros*. God's point: this creature's strength serves no human purpose.

**v.13 — "the wing of the ostriches":** The Hebrew *kanaf-renanim* is difficult. *Renanim* may relate to joyful cries. The ostrich passage (vv.13-18) is unique in God's speech — the ostrich is presented not as a marvel of wisdom but as a creature that lacks it, yet still thrives and outpaces the horse.

**v.19-25 — The warhorse:** One of the most celebrated animal portraits in ancient literature. The horse does not merely endure battle — it delights in it. The phrase *he'ach* ("Aha!") gives the horse a voice of eager anticipation.

*— EMET*
